title: analysis.opportunity.arbitration.v1
description: Published by analysis-engine's internal/arbitration package whenever a live opportunity's cross-strategy conflict-resolution status changes for its symbol (docs/adr/004-analysis-engine-owns-arbitration-and-technique.md). Deliberately a separate, small, frequently-republished topic rather than a field on analysis.opportunity.v1: that topic's Created-event-happens-once contract is load-bearing for algo-bot's idempotent match-write logic, while arbitration status is a time-varying relationship between candidates that changes independently of any single candidate's own lifecycle (a new candidate on one timeframe can flip an already-published candidate's status on another without that candidate itself re-evaluating — see internal/engine's SymbolWorker.arbitrate doc comment). Consumers should treat decided_at as a monotonic freshness check and discard a stale/reordered event, the same way analysis_client.freshness already does for opportunity envelopes — this event carries no ledger/outbox de-duplication guarantee beyond at-least-once delivery, since republishing the same decision is harmless by design. This is the PAYLOAD only — wrapped inside contracts/common/event-envelope-v1.schema.json's `payload` field.

opportunity_id.description: Matches the id field of the analysis.opportunity.v1 event this decision is about.

status.description: winner: this candidate is the current arbitrated pick for its direction. suppressed: ranked lower (same direction) or on the losing side of a decisive opposite-direction resolution. conflict_held: an opposite-direction rival is not decisively weaker; the whole symbol holds rather than picking a side. uncontested: the only live candidate for this symbol right now.

reason_code.description: Shared across every Decision one Arbitrate call returns — describes the batch outcome, not a per-candidate property (internal/arbitration.ReasonCode).

conflicting_with.description: Present only when status is conflict_held: the opportunity_ids of the opposing-direction candidates this decision was held against.

decided_at.description: Unix seconds — the closed bar's time that produced this Arbitrate() evaluation, not wall-clock publish time.
